judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Pictograms' (Sub-Theme Data Collection and Presentation). The first objective is to identify the most common feature of a pictogram (the mode); the second is to mention the usefulness of the pictogram (the mode). Being able to identify the mode is a concrete skill that supports the more interpretive task of articulating its usefulness, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second. Same-rank direction is justified by this substantive skill-to-application progression (source objective ordering 3 then 4), not merely shared hierarchy or token overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two (rank 1) Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) and Sub-Theme (Shapes). The first identifies 2D shapes (square, rectangle, circle, triangle); the second identifies real-world home objects that are cuboids/cubes (3D shapes). They are complementary shape-identification skills within one shape strand, giving substantive conceptual coherence, but the evidence does not establish a directional dependency: they sit in distinct parallel topics (Topic 2 Two-dimensional vs Topic 1 Three-dimensional) at the same grade rank with no source support that 2D identification is required for 3D object recognition. relatesTo best fits; same-rank buildsTowards lacks substantive developmental evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Number and Numeration) and Sub-Theme (Whole Number), but sit in distinct topics: 'use idea of place value limited to tens and units' (Topic 4, Whole number 10) and 'identify and read correctly the numbers 1-99' (Topic 5, Whole Numbers 1-99). They share substantive conceptual coherence in whole-number numeration—place value of tens/units and reading two-digit numbers mutually reinforce one another. Both are at the same coordinate rank (0), and the evidence does not clearly establish which objective developmentally supports the other, so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted. Token/trigram overlap is largely generic scaffolding ('pupil should be able to'), not decisive. relatesTo best captures the complementary skill coherence.
